advisory.title: `libsqlite3-sys` via C SQLite CVE-2026-119375
advisory.description:
SQLite versions before 3.54.0 can return uninitialized page-cache memory when a process opens a database file together with a sibling write-ahead-log (`-wal`) file whose page size differs from the database's. A crafted pair of files can make ordinary queries return stale bytes from the process's memory. The attack vector is local and needs the victim to open the files.

As `libsqlite3-sys` bundles SQLite when it is built from its bundled source (the `bundled` feature, which `rusqlite`'s `bundled` feature enables), it is susceptible to the vulnerability. The releases `0.6.0` to `0.38.2` bundle SQLite `3.13.0` to `3.53.2` and are affected; the earlier releases contain no SQLite source. `libsqlite3-sys` was updated to bundle the patched version of SQLite in `0.39.0` (SQLite `3.54.0`) and `0.39.1` (SQLite `3.54.1`), released with [`rusqlite` 0.41](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite/releases/tag/v0.41.0). `libsqlite3-sys` `0.39` declares Rust 1.88 and `rusqlite` `0.41` declares Rust 1.89.

Only a process that opens a database file, with its `-wal`, that a less trusted party could have written is exposed. A build that links a system SQLite instead of the bundled source is not affected by the copy in this crate; its exposure is that of the system library's version. The `bundled-sqlcipher` feature builds SQLCipher instead of SQLite; in `0.39.0` and `0.39.1` it depends on `sqlcipher-src =419.0.6`, which bundles SQLite `3.53.4` and is affected.

advisory.title: paste - no longer maintained
advisory.description:
The creator of the crate `paste` has stated in the [`README.md`](https://github.com/dtolnay/paste/blob/master/README.md) 
that this project is not longer maintained as well as archived the repository

## Possible Alternative(s)

- [`pastey`]: a fork of paste and is aimed to be a drop-in replacement with additional features for paste crate
- [`with_builtin_macros`]: crate providing a [superset of `paste`'s functionality including general `macro_rules!` eager expansions](https://docs.rs/with_builtin_macros/0.1.0/with_builtin_macros/macro.with_eager_expansions.html)  and `concat!`/`concat_idents!` macros

[`pastey`]: https://crates.io/crates/pastey
[`with_builtin_macros`]: https://crates.io/crates/with_builtin_macros

advisory.title: proc-macro-error2 is unmaintained
advisory.description:
The author of `proc-macro-error2` has [confirmed](https://github.com/GnomedDev/proc-macro-error-2/issues/17#issuecomment-4643215473) that the crate is no longer maintained and recommends that users migrate away from it.

`proc-macro-error2` was originally created as a maintained fork of [`proc-macro-error`](https://crates.io/crates/proc-macro-error) (see [RUSTSEC-2024-0370](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0370)). Both the original crate and this fork are now unmaintained.

## Possible Alternative(s)

- [manyhow](https://crates.io/crates/manyhow)
- [proc-macro2-diagnostics](https://github.com/SergioBenitez/proc-macro2-diagnostics)

advisory.title: `ttf-parser` is unmaintained
advisory.description:
The author of `ttf-parser` has stated that the crate is unmaintained and will not receive further fixes (see the referenced issue).

## Alternative(s)

- [`skrifa`](https://crates.io/crates/skrifa), an actively maintained TrueType and OpenType font parsing crate, part of the Google Fonts "oxidize" (`fontations`) project.

advisory.title: `event-listener` allows `!Send` tags to cross thread boundaries via `StackSlot`
advisory.description:
Affected versions of `event-listener` unconditionally implement `Send` and
`Sync` for `StackSlot<'_, T>`, the stack-allocated listener type created
by the `listener!` macro.

This allows a `!Send` tag type set via `Event::with_tag` to be moved to
another thread and accessed via `StackSlot::wait`, causing a data race in safe
code.

advisory.title: `AsyncFd::new` and related constructors violate I/O safety
advisory.description:
`tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd` provides safe constructors (`new`, `with_interest`, `try_new`, and `try_with_interest`) that accept any `T: AsRawFd` rather than requiring proof of ownership or validity of the file descriptor. Because `RawFd` implements `AsRawFd`, safe code can construct an `AsyncFd` from an arbitrary or closed file descriptor, or close/replace the underlying file descriptor while the `AsyncFd` is still alive.

This violates I/O safety in two ways:

1. `AsyncFd<T>` implements `AsFd` for all `T: AsRawFd` by calling `BorrowedFd::borrow_raw(self.as_raw_fd())`, allowing safe code to obtain an arbitrary `BorrowedFd<'_>` without owning the file descriptor.
2. Tokio's I/O driver stores a pointer to an internal allocation in the `epoll`/`kqueue` user data for registered file descriptors. If the underlying file descriptor is duplicated and then closed while an `AsyncFd` is alive, and the OS reuses that file descriptor number for a another IO resource on the same runtime, dropping the first `AsyncFd` deregisters the reused file descriptor number and frees the first while the original file description remains registered in `epoll`, leading to a use-after-free when a readiness event fires.

Starting in Tokio 1.51.6, 1.53.3, and 1.54.0, `AsyncFd::new`, `AsyncFd::with_interest`, `AsyncFd::try_new`, and `AsyncFd::try_with_interest` are deprecated in favor of the `unsafe` constructors `AsyncFd::register` and `AsyncFd::register_with_interest`. Callers must ensure that the file descriptor remains valid, open, and unchanged for the lifetime of the `AsyncFd`.
